S.FORM: Namuk nen̄, o m̄arat tuwal mätän na-mon o raqa.
S.TRANSL: Here's my story: once upon a time there was a man and his wife.

S.FORM: Ru m-sasag nen̄ va– van, ti ru wokem na-moru tuar o guvur.
S.TRANSL: They were living together, and one day they decided to build themselves a house.

S.FORM: Wokem bas moru (o) guvur, v-van tar da-tkōr, v-van ma, v-vēn, sē rru v-tōv.
S.TRANSL: So they built a house, went to cut some sago leaves, brought them back, and began sewing them together for the roof.

S.FORM: Ru mō-tōv bas, titi v-ron̄ kak van tar o bō.
S.TRANSL: Once the roof thatch was ready, they decided to go cut the bamboo.

S.FORM: M-van sa nen̄ le-vwon, ru v-tar o bō titi, m-tar a–van titi na-mon o raqa ron̄: “Wē! Ēl ka nen̄ mē! Tuar o bō t-tur ti llon nen̄, o qätgi.”
S.TRANSL: So they walked into the bush, and began cutting bamboos. “Hey!” the woman suddenly exclaimed, “Look this way! This bamboo in the middle is really large.”

S.FORM: Ti na-mon o m̄arat ron̄ “Tuqa, na s-van sur na s-tar.”
S.TRANSL: “Wait,” replied her husband, “let me cut it down.”

S.FORM: M-van sag, van sag wa ni m-tar, titi ni m-ron̄ ēs wor ma le bō nen̄ titi “Tartar tiktik wor! Ēlgor nēk s-tar wēs na!”
S.TRANSL: So he came close to the bamboo and started cutting it, when suddenly he heard a voice coming out of the bamboo: “Cut slowly! Make sure you don't cut me!”

S.FORM: Titi na-mon o m̄arat nen̄ ron̄ “Ēy! Na m-ron̄ m̄ar wa sē valvalaw le bō ne.”
S.TRANSL: “Hey!” said the man, “I think I just heard someone talk in this bamboo!”

S.FORM: Titi na-mon o raqa nen̄ ron̄ “Tuar togo ka m-valvalaw le bō nen̄. Du s-tar wa du s-tar tus tuar qalē tävtēn, du s-tar tus tun tuar qalē meken.”
S.TRANSL: His wife replied “It was a child talking inside that bamboo! Let's cut the bamboo at the knot right below, and on the knot right above.”

S.FORM: Titi na-mon o m̄arat nen̄ m-van, m-tar, m-van mē ma, sē ru v-säqäl.
S.TRANSL: So the man chopped the bamboo stem, took it down, and they started to split it open.

S.FORM: Säqäl o bō nen̄, m-ēl ēs wor, ti o togo t-sag ti llon.
S.TRANSL: When they split it, they discovered a child inside.

S.FORM: Titi o raqa nen̄ ron̄ “Awō! I-ntōndu ne!”
S.TRANSL: “Heavens!” said the woman, “we now have a child!”

S.FORM: Titi na-mon o m̄arat ron̄ “O sa?” Ni ron̄ “O m̄arat! Tuar togo m̄arat!”
S.TRANSL: “What?” said her husband – “It's a boy,” she replied, “it's a small boy!”

S.FORM: Titi, ni ron̄ “Du s-wes na-ssan i Wuwut Matdon̄.”
S.TRANSL: “We will give him the name Wuwut Matdong, ‘Gorgeous Boy’.”

S.FORM: Titi na-mon o tudun nen̄ ron̄ “V-wē, nēk s-gorväg ni na soltäg o ōtōt bō nen̄. Ti duru mōl kēl mi ni gatam. Nēk t-tōr wōswōs o bō v-ēlgor o bō s-m̄em̄sän̄ na-ben!”
S.TRANSL: “Alright,” the husband added, “you carry him in your arms, while I [get rid? of] those pieces of bamboo as we bring him back to our home. You shouldn't handle the bamboo, it might graze his skin.”

S.FORM: Titi ru v-mōl. 🌿
S.TRANSL: So they went home. 🌿

S.FORM: Mōl ror nen̄, ru vō-kkōr ni vō-kkōr ni a–van, ni t-risris ti, va–van ni t-turtur malgo ti.
S.TRANSL: From that day on, they took care of the boy. Time went by, and soon he was able to crawl on all fours; a while later, he could stand firmly on his own.

S.FORM: Va–van, ni ron̄ “Auu! I-ntōndu nen̄ ni t-qatgi nok ti.”
S.TRANSL: The parents would marvel at how fast he would grow.

S.FORM: A–van ni t-vanvan ti.
S.TRANSL: One day he started to walk.

S.FORM: Vanvan a–van ti ni o qatgi lōmgäv ka nok.
S.TRANSL: And then he soon became a big boy.

S.FORM: Titi ru t-mōrōs wōs mē ron̄ kak ni kak v-vanvan bērē le-vwon, ni kak sasag wor l-guvur.
S.TRANSL: Yet they didn't want him to walk alone in the bush, they wanted him to just stay at home.

S.FORM: Ni v-mōrōs kak ni v-van le-vwon, la i-vveru t-mōrōs wōs mē ni v-van le-vwon.
S.TRANSL: Every time he asked if he could go out in the forest, his mother would refuse.

S.FORM: Titi, na-mor o naw m-bas, titi ni ron̄ “La ma o bō nen̄, na s-van täv na-mēgēn o naw.”
S.TRANSL: One day, as they were running out of salt water, he said “Give me the bamboo bottle, I'll go fetch some water myself.”

S.FORM: Ron̄ “Bek! Nēk mētē sēwsēw bērē, nēk sēw ror nen̄ lorlorqa nēr ka t-sag ti lo-on nen̄, ru s-rot marmar nēk.”
S.TRANSL: “No way!” they replied, “If you walk down to the sea on your own, you'll be held captive by two girls on the beach!”

S.FORM: A–van, i-vveru v-sēwēl wor o naw nen̄.
S.TRANSL: So his mother walked down to the shore to fetch water herself.

S.FORM: M-van mē ma, tēlēr m-sasag a–van, mē-tēlēr o naw m-bas mala.
S.TRANSL: But then, it was not long before they ran out of salt water again.

S.FORM: Ti ni ron̄ “Na s-sēw sur.”
S.TRANSL: “Let me go!” said Wuwut.

S.FORM: Ron̄ “Bek, sēwsēw bērē! Ēlo lorlorqa irō nen̄ s-rot marmar nēk.”
S.TRANSL: “No, you can't go!” they replied. “Otherwise you'll find there two girls who'll hold you captive!”

S.FORM: Ti la ni v-marmar, sē ni v-sēw. 🌿 🌿
S.TRANSL: But this time he insisted so much, that he was the one to go. 🌿 🌿

S.FORM: Ni m-sēw ror, ni m-sēw ror, ni m-sēw ror, kak ni s-täv o naw, ni m-ēl ēs wor lorlorqa irō v-gintäg ma.
S.TRANSL: So he went out, and walked all the way down to the shore to fetch some salt water. Suddenly he saw two women running to him.

S.FORM: Tuar m-tur tavlōn laman, tuar m-tur tavlōn laman. Ron̄ “Na-momär o m̄arat inēk! Nēk t-mōl kēl wōswōs, tēlēn s-n̄or!”
S.TRANSL: One took his left hand, the other took his right hand. “You're our husband!” they said, “You can't go back now: come and sleep with us!”

S.FORM: Titi o togo nen̄ ron̄: “Iō! Qiri ka ne o län̄vus luwo. Qatgi län̄vus s-daw gēn qiri l-qōn̄.”
S.TRANSL: After a moment, the boy said: “I'm afraid there's going to be a hurricane today. Tonight in fact, we'll be hit by a massive hurricane.”

S.FORM: Ron̄ “Kumur v-ron̄ mē o di vätäl, le bek?”
S.TRANSL: Then he asked: “You know what banana trees are, don't you?”

S.FORM: Ru ron̄ “E! Kämär v-ron̄ o di vätäl.” Ron̄ “Ar van kot ma!”
S.TRANSL: “Of course!” they replied “we know what banana trees are.” — “Then go cut me one!”

S.FORM: M-van sa nen̄, kot ma o di vätäl i-tuwal, van mē ma, ron̄: “Kumur s-van kumur s-kot o derde rga; kumur s-van ma kumur s-buläs marmar na-mētēlēn o guvur, s-ran̄ o wetga, s-van ma s-lēg marmar, sur qiri ka ne qatgi län̄vus.”
S.TRANSL: So they both went out, found a banana trunk and brought it back. Then he went on: “Now I want you to go cut some leaves, and I want you to prepare a stable protection for our thatch roofs; you will need to find vines and tie them firmly: we have to prepare for tonight's big hurricane.”

S.FORM: Titi, ni ron̄ “Kumur s-van, kumur s-vut ma o wiswisi o dävlō, kumur s-van mē ma, kumur s-lavtati.”
S.TRANSL: “Finally”, he added, “you will have to pluck some palm leaves, bring them here, and put them down.”

S.FORM: Ti, ru m-van ēl bas, ru m-van ma, lavtati.
S.TRANSL: So they went to find some palm leaves, brought them and put them down.

S.FORM: V-rävräv, tēlēr m-gängän bas tēlēr. V-n̄or. 🌿
S.TRANSL: In the evening, the three of them had dinner together, and went to sleep. 🌿

S.FORM: Tēlēr m-n̄or bas, titi m-n̄or n̄or n̄or a–van, v-ron̄ ēs wor titi lorlorqa irō ne tō-n̄ōrsēg nok ti.
S.TRANSL: While they were in bed, he waited till the two girls were fast asleep.

S.FORM: Titi, lorlorqa irō nen̄ m-gorväg marmar ni, m-qäg na-ron̄oru meken, la ni m-n̄or vititnē.
S.TRANSL: He was lying in the middle, with the girls on both sides embracing him firmly, their legs wrapped around his body.

S.FORM: I-at ne m-la tiktik wor den na-lamaru, ror, le-tamn̄a. Titi ru v-savut ma o di vätäl ne, tul ti l-vititnē, m-qäg kēl vak na-lamaru, sōkō wonwon kēl iru, tēlēr v-n̄or.
S.TRANSL: So he started to remove their arms very gently, and put them down on the bed. Then he seized the trunk of the banana tree, which he placed right between them; then he lifted their arms and laid them back there; tucked them in a cover, and let them to sleep together.

S.FORM: Ru tō-dōm ti ak i va ne, kak t-n̄or mē iru ti la ni vi-bek nok.
S.TRANSL: They thought that was him in the middle, lying with them, when in fact he was already gone!

S.FORM: Ni m-suwäg o wiswisi o dävlō i-rō ti l-deln̄an; la t-märän rorwor ka nok ti.
S.TRANSL: He rolled two palm leaves and stuck them above his ears; then he realised the day was already dawning.

S.FORM: Ti ni m-van ror bet o naw ka kirm̄ōt ma ti.
S.TRANSL: He walked towards the waves that were breaking on the shore.

S.FORM: Titi ni ron̄: “Ey!” / Varvar tal iru nen̄, ron̄ “Ey! Ar van ka nen̄ ma!”
S.TRANSL: “Hey!” he said, waking up the two girls: “Now come this way!”

S.FORM: Rarm̄er ne v-durun̄ ēl ēs ror nen̄ ti ni t-tur nok ti le naw.
S.TRANSL: They watched him as he was standing there, near the sea.

S.FORM: Ti ni vit min iru ron̄: “Kumur wa na m-sēwēl ror ma o naw, ti kumur v-mōrōs kak kumur vit ron̄ kak na-momur o m̄arat kak ina, la v-wē, na s-mōl kēl wor kumur v-sag tavul kēl wor nok tene.”
S.TRANSL: Then he declared to them: “When I came down to fetch some salt water, you said you wanted me to become your husband. Sorry, but now I'm going away, you'll have to stay here without me.”

S.FORM: La ni t-valvalaw titi, na-ron̄on nen̄ o gele mäs nok.
S.TRANSL: As he spoke, his legs had already turned into a fish tail.

S.FORM: Valvalaw va–van, la i-vven ka m-van ma, tēlēr v-ron̄ ni ti: / m-gintäg kēl sag, ron̄ “Ēy! Van ka nen̄ ma, i-ntōndu ror ne o mäs m-van dēn̄ nok sag un kere qolon.”
S.TRANSL: Suddenly his mother arrived, saw him, and rushed back up to her home, saying “Come with me, our son has transformed into a fish, from his feet up to his hips!”

S.FORM: M-van sag, m-vit ni, m-van ma, ru m-ēl bas wor ni, ti i-at ne ron̄: “Kumur v-sag, kumur v-sag nok te nen̄, era mam mētän i-vōvō v-sag wor sa nen̄ na s-mōl.”
S.TRANSL: They both hurried down to see him, but then he said: “O ladies, please just stay there; o Dad and Mum, please just stay there.”

S.FORM: Sē ni m-solqäg kal tal m̄ar nen̄, sē ni v-gav ror nen̄ l-sele.
S.TRANSL: Suddenly he took a big leap in the air like this, and glided his way down into the lagoon!

S.FORM: Titi, i-mam namon v-mōrōs kak v-ēl ni.
S.TRANSL: But his father was desperate to see him again.

S.FORM: Ni m-sa sēw ror l-masle bē, ni m-tar tuar o rän̄, m-ran̄ tuar gēdurta, m-van ror, me-rev namon o ak bō sē ni v-sō.
S.TRANSL: So he rushed to the river, found some crayfish, picked a long vine; then he hurried back to the shore, dragged his bamboo raft and put it out to sea.

S.FORM: V-sō ror nen̄, l-sele / siliakem [dunn̄äg] ror o rän̄ nen̄. Dundunn̄äg o va nen̄, o rän̄.
S.TRANSL: Paddling his way into the lagoon, he began to lower the crayfish. Using the vine as a rope, he lowered the crayfish into the water.

S.FORM: Titi, ni m-ron̄ ēs wor ti ni v-sokem ni.
S.TRANSL: At some point he felt he was striking the fish.

S.FORM: Titi, ni v-rev. M-rev rev va–––van, titi ni ron̄ “Nēk v-mōrōs kak i nēk v-ēl kēl na-mon̄ i-vōvō? Nēk v-vit tavul!”
S.TRANSL: So he pulled. He pulled it up, up, up, then he said: “Would you like to see your Mum again? Tell me the truth!”

S.FORM: Ti ni ron̄ “Nēk v-sasag nok tene, na v-sō vil kēl ni.”
S.TRANSL: “Alright,” he added, “just stay there, and I'll go fetch her.”

S.FORM: M-sō sag, m-van min ni ror, m-ērēt kal wor den sag le naw. Tuwa bas wor na-moru o äs / tuwa bas wor na-moru o äs min iru.
S.TRANSL: He paddled back to his wife, brought her back: the fish was there, with just its head above the surface. Then it began singing a song for his parents: yes, he sang them a song.

S.FORM: Titi ni ron̄ “Kumur s-mōl kēl wor, titi kumur sag gor na-lulsik.”
S.TRANSL: And finally, he concluded: “Dad and Mum, please return home now; go back and look after my place in your home.”

S.FORM: Ne ēn wor le. O ususräg bēlē maraw.
S.TRANSL: That's it. This was my story.
